T-001.threat: Secure Boot bypass — attacker bypasses cryptographic boot chain verification
T-001.cause: Secure Boot is not enforced — unsigned firmware can execute
T-001.attack: Attacker loads malicious firmware that bypasses Secure Boot verification

T-002.threat: Firmware readback — attacker extracts firmware image from the chip
T-002.cause: Firmware readback protection not enabled — flash memory is readable via debug interface
T-002.attack: Attacker connects to debug interface and reads flash memory to extract the complete firmware image

T-003.threat: Counterfeit chip insertion — attacker substitutes genuine chip with malicious version
T-003.cause: No supply chain verification — chips cannot be authenticated
T-003.attack: Attacker introduces counterfeit chips containing hardware backdoors into the supply chain

T-004.threat: Embedded process firmware tampering — attacker modifies firmware of embedded process component
T-004.cause: No cryptographic code signing on embedded process firmware
T-004.attack: Attacker replaces embedded process firmware to disable security checks or introduce a backdoor

T-005.threat: Embedded storage tampering — attacker modifies data in non-volatile memory
T-005.cause: Flash/EEPROM/NVRAM storage lacks access control or integrity protection
T-005.attack: Attacker uses debug interface to modify firmware, configuration, or calibration data

T-006.threat: OT protocol data tampering — attacker modifies data on OT protocol stack
T-006.cause: OT protocol stack carries no integrity protection
T-006.attack: Attacker intercepts OT protocol messages and modifies setpoints or process values

T-007.threat: Embedded firmware tampering — attacker modifies firmware on embedded controller
T-007.cause: No cryptographic code signing enforced — unsigned firmware is accepted for execution
T-007.attack: Attacker replaces firmware with a malicious version that disables safety interlocks

T-008.threat: Configuration tampering on embedded system — attacker modifies stored configuration
T-008.cause: Configuration storage lacks integrity protection — parameters can be modified without detection
T-008.attack: Attacker modifies safety-critical configuration parameters stored on the embedded system

T-009.threat: Physical cable tampering — data flow manipulated via accessible cable or connector
T-009.cause: Data flow runs through a physically accessible cable without physical protection
T-009.attack: Attacker splices in a tap device or signal injector and manipulates data in transit without triggering any alarm

T-010.threat: Integrity attack on safety-relevant data flow — false values reach safety function
T-010.cause: Safety-critical data flow carries no end-to-end integrity protection
T-010.attack: Attacker modifies values on the safety data flow causing the safety function to operate on false data

T-011.threat: Unauthorized write access via OT protocol — attacker modifies process values or configuration
T-011.cause: OT protocol data flow is configured with read-write access — any node can issue write commands without authorization
T-011.attack: Attacker places a rogue node on the OT network and sends write commands to modify setpoints or controller configuration

T-012.threat: Shared-memory race / TOCTOU — concurrent access corrupts or bypasses validated data
T-012.cause: Access to shared memory or MMIO registers between cores/tasks is not synchronized (no lock, atomic, or memory barrier)
T-012.attack: An attacker or fault on one master modifies the region between another master's check and use, corrupting state or bypassing a validation

T-013.threat: Memory isolation bypass (write) — protected region writable across privilege domains
T-013.cause: The MPU/MMU region for the shared memory or MMIO block is misconfigured — write isolation between domains is not enforced
T-013.attack: A low-privilege task writes a protected region, injecting commands or corrupting another domain's data
